main_text.p: stentias. Ubi à duobus victus formam inuestigare docet, nempe à virtute & morbi constitutione, in qua morbi dispositionem & status distantiam comprehendit. Cuius verba ita habent: Τὸ μὲν τ' ὅλως διαίτης χῡμα πᾶς σνο σκοπὸς ἐκ βλέπων ἐποιεῖτο, τῇ τε διαίτα μιᾷ τῷ κάμνοντι, καὶ τῶν κατα̈στασιν τῷ νο σήματ’. τὸ γὰρ εἴτε κάτοξυ, εἴτε ὀξὺ, εἴτε χρό νιον ἐσοῖ τὸ νόσημα, καὶ ὁπλωίνα μάλιστα τῇ ἀκμὴν ἐκλήψεις, τῶν κατα̈στασιν ὅσι τ' νοσή ματ’ σκοπῆι. Hoc est, Totius victus formam duos respiciens scopos instituit, ægrotantis nempe virtutem & morbi constitutionem. Illud enim, siue peracutus, siue acutus, siue chronicus morbus erit, & quando maxime in statu consistet, constitutionem morbi est considerare. Unde male quidam vertit hunc locum in hunc modum: Nam si morbus sit peracutus, vel acutus, vel longus, &c. qui verborum sensum corrupit & non transtulit. Ex quibus verbis duo sub constitutionis nomine comprehendisse Hippocratem, nempe morbi acumen, & status distantiam, aperte ostendit.

page.notes: The Greek passage is printed with many irregular accents and letters; readings are approximate. Left-margin "„" marks are printed quotation marks, not notes. Catchword and signature absent.
